title: Solve it together: find the biggest with a helper
idea: GUIDED (UEPCC). Decompose 'highest value' into a biggest(nums) helper using the track pattern (best starts at first item), with a one-item sanity check. No max() builtin.
problem: Temperatures are [12, 19, 7, 15]. Show the highest, using a biggest(nums) helper.

exercises.prompt:
PROBLEM: temperatures [12, 19, 7, 15]. Show the highest, using biggest(nums).

OUTPUT?
exercises.explanation: Output = the single highest value. We'll track it as we walk the list.
Input is the list. The helper walks it and keeps the best seen so far.

exercises.prompt: Example — by hand. Walking [12, 19, 7, 15], the biggest is...
exercises.explanation: 19 beats 12, 7, and 15. Hand answer = 19, our check value.

exercises.prompt: To find the biggest WITHOUT max(), we start 'best' at the first item and update it when we see something larger.
exercises.explanation: Yes — that's the track pattern. best = nums[0], then raise best whenever a bigger value appears.

exercises.prompt: Plan — which pattern finds the highest value?
options: Track the biggest (keep a 'best so far' and update it)
exercises.explanation: Track-the-biggest: carry a best-so-far and replace it when a larger value shows up.

blocks: Set best to the first item
Look at each item in turn
If an item is bigger than best, make it the new best
exercises.explanation: Start best at the first item, walk the rest, raise best on anything larger, return it.

exercises.prompt: Code the helper and use it.
exercises.explanation: best starts at nums[0], the loop raises it when n is larger, then return. We compute the max ourselves — no builtin.
We replace best only when the new item is greater, so the operator is >.

exercises.prompt: Check — the code prints 19; hand example was 19. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Output (19) matches the hand-worked 19. The track helper is correct.

exercises.prompt: Re-check with one item: biggest([5]). What should it return?
options: 5 — the only item is the biggest
exercises.explanation: With one item, best = nums[0] = 5 and the loop finds nothing larger. A single-item list is handled correctly.
